title: Effective fppf descent of quasi-coherent modules on algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and small sites in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\{q_i:X_i\to X\}_{i\in I}$ be a small fppf covering: the maps are flat and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts and jointly surjective [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus]. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed sites [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], tensor pullback and module morphisms [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. A descent datum consists of modules $M_i\in\operatorname{QCoh}(X_i)$ and isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}:\operatorname{pr}_i^*M_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{pr}_j^*M_j$ on $X_i\times_X X_j$, such that $\varphi_{ik}=\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}$ on every triple fibre product, with canonical pullback composition comparisons understood. A morphism of descent data consists of maps $a_i:M_i\to N_i$ satisfying $\varphi^N_{ij}\circ\operatorname{pr}_i^*a_i=\operatorname{pr}_j^*a_j\circ\varphi^M_{ij}$. The canonical functor from $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ to this category, sending $M$ to $(q_i^*M,\mathrm{can})$, is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Equivalently every such datum is effective, and compatible maps descend uniquely. No quasi-compactness, separatedness, Noetherian or finite-generation hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 04W8, proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent, specialized to fppf coverings; spaces-topologies.tex Tag 0DFQ, lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc, shows such coverings are fpqc.

proof.text: Use tensor pullbacks throughout. They preserve quasi-coherence for arbitrary space morphisms, so the canonical functor $K$ and all pullbacks below have the required quasi-coherent values. Use the normalized composition maps: locally $a\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto a f^\sharp(b)\otimes m$. Both associations of three successive pullbacks send $a\otimes(b\otimes(c\otimes m))$ to $a f^\sharp(b)(gf)^\sharp(c)\otimes m$; the unit maps send $a\otimes m$ to $am$. Thus all composition and identity identifications used below obey the same associativity and unit equations. On schemes use the Zariski/etale equivalence, including its comparison for every scheme morphism, to apply ordinary scheme descent; no direct-image comparison is used.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), steps (1),(3),(4); pullback normalization and scheme comparison before applying 023T.

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $e_i:A_i\to X_i$ for each $i$. The composites $r_i=q_ie_i:A_i\to X$ are an fppf family by etale-to-fppf comparison and composition. For any scheme $t:T\to X$, set $B_i(T)=T\times_XA_i$, with projections $b_i:B_i(T)\to T$ and $d_i:B_i(T)\to A_i$. These are schemes by representability of the diagonal, even though $t$ need not be etale. Base change makes $\{b_i\}$ an fppf covering of schemes, hence an fpqc covering. The same applies to every scheme test and every iterated overlap used below. All families remain small; no finite subcover of $X$ or quasi-compact atlas is chosen.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), step (3), refine the sources by scheme atlases, and step (4), pull back to scheme tests; spaces-topologies 03Y9 and topologies 022C.

proof.text: For a datum $\xi=(M_i,\varphi_{ij})$, give $B_i(T)$ the module $L_i(T)=(e_id_i)^*M_i$. On $B_i(T)\times_TB_j(T)$ use the pullback of $\varphi_{ij}$ along its map to $X_i\times_XX_j$ as the transition. The original triple equation pulls back to the triple equation for these modules, so this is scheme descent data. Scheme fpqc descent gives $H_T(\xi)\in\operatorname{QCoh}(T)$ and isomorphisms $\theta_{T,i}:b_i^*H_T(\xi)\simeq L_i(T)$ respecting those transitions. In particular on overlaps $\theta_{T,j}=\varphi_{ij}\theta_{T,i}$, with all maps pulled back there. Retain these specified isomorphisms as part of the descent object. This construction is made for scheme tests in the fixed universe; only a small chart skeleton is needed to assemble a sheaf.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), step (4), application of scheme Tag 023T; retain the descent identifications.

proof.text: For any scheme map $f:T'\to T$ over $X$, let $f_i:B_i(T')\to B_i(T)$ be its base change. The covered map from $b_i'^*f^*H_T$ to $b_i'^*H_{T'}$ is $\theta_{T',i}^{-1}f_i^*\theta_{T,i}$. On double overlaps its compatibility square reduces, after conjugating by the two $\theta$'s, to the equality between the pullback of $\varphi_{ij}$ along $f$ and the transition defining $L_i(T')$. Full faithfulness of scheme descent therefore gives a unique $c_f:f^*H_T\simeq H_{T'}$; the inverses descend by the inverse square. For $f=1$ the covered map is the identity. For $g:T''\to T'$, the covered composite $c_g g^*c_f$ is $\theta_{T'',i}^{-1}(fg)_i^*\theta_{T,i}$ by cancellation of $g_i^*\theta_{T',i}$. Faithfulness gives $c_1=1$ and $c_{fg}=c_g g^*c_f$. Crucially, this construction includes maps between scheme tests that are not etale over $X$.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), step (6), omitted compatibility with scheme morphisms, expanded by scheme descent full faithfulness.

proof.text: A morphism $a:\xi\to\zeta$ gives maps $L_i(T,\xi)\to L_i(T,\zeta)$ by pulling back $a_i$. The morphism-of-data equation in the statement says exactly that these maps respect the overlap transitions. Descend them to $H_T(a)$ using full faithfulness. For $f:T'\to T$, the transition square for $H_T(a)$ becomes the square for the same pulled-back $a_i$ on $B_i(T')$, hence commutes by faithfulness. Identities and composites descend to identities and composites for the same reason. Restricting $(H_T,c_f)$ to the etale scheme charts of $X$, the cartesian-chart equivalence now supplies a quasi-coherent module $B(\xi)$, with compatible isomorphisms $\rho_U:u^*B(\xi)\simeq H_U$ on each chart $u:U\to X$. It also supplies the maps $B(a)$, making $B$ a functor.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), steps (5),(6), omitted functoriality in the datum and chartwise assembly; spaces-properties 03LY and 03LZ.

proof.text: We need the comparison on a scheme test $t:T\to X$ that is not necessarily etale. Choose an etale scheme atlas $u:U\to X$ and put $W=T\times_XU$, $a:W\to U$, $b:W\to T$. The map $b$ is a surjective etale scheme map. On $W$ define $b^*t^*B(\xi)\to b^*H_T$ by $c_b^{-1}c_a a^*\rho_U$. On $W\times_TW$, let $a_1,a_2$ be its maps to $U$. They factor through $R=U\times_XU$. Compatibility of $\rho$ on the etale charts $U,R$ and the identity $c_{fg}=c_g g^*c_f$ make the two displayed maps equal: both become $c_{b\pi}^{-1}c_{a_1\pi_1}(a_1\pi_1)^*\rho_U$, using the chart transition on $R$ to replace the second $U$ projection by the first. Scheme etale/fpqc descent descends this map and its inverse uniquely to $\lambda_T:t^*B(\xi)\simeq H_T$. For $f:T'\to T$, pull the claimed equality $\lambda_{T'}=c_f f^*\lambda_T$ back along $T'\times_XU\to T'$. Substitution of the displayed formula and cancellation of $c_b$ give that equality. The same substitution proves naturality in $\xi$. For an etale chart $T$, this comparison is $\rho_T$, by its chart compatibility and uniqueness.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), steps (6),(7), chart assembly compared with arbitrary tensor pullback; omitted inverse verification, expanded using etale localization and 023T.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and an etale scheme chart $v:V\to X_i$; write $t=q_iv$. On the scheme fpqc cover $B_j(V)=V\times_XA_j\to V$, the pullback of $\varphi_{ij}$ identifies the pullback of $v^*M_i$ with $L_j(V)$. Hence the maps $\varphi_{ij}^{-1}\theta_{V,j}$ identify the pullbacks of $H_V$ with those of $v^*M_i$. On a double overlap the required equality is $\varphi_{ik}^{-1}\varphi_{jk}=\varphi_{ij}^{-1}$, which follows by multiplying the original triple equation by inverses. Full faithfulness of scheme descent gives an isomorphism $\eta_V:H_V\simeq v^*M_i$. For a map $h:V'\to V$ over $X_i$, the covered formulas give $\eta_{V'}c_h=h^*\eta_V$, so this equality holds by faithfulness. The maps $\eta_V\lambda_V:v^*q_i^*B(\xi)\simeq v^*M_i$ thus form compatible chart maps. The cartesian-chart equivalence on $X_i$ assembles them into $\alpha_i:q_i^*B(\xi)\simeq M_i$. Their construction is natural in $\xi$.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), step (7), recovery of the original components, including descent along the source atlases rather than assuming refinement is an equivalence.

proof.text: The maps $\alpha_i$ respect the original, unrefined datum. Indeed, take any etale scheme chart $V\to X_i\times_XX_j$ and then its scheme fpqc cover $B_k(V)\to V$. Naturality of $\lambda$ and $\eta$ identifies the two maps from the pullback of $B(\xi)$ to the pullback of $M_j$ with $\varphi_{ij}\varphi_{ik}^{-1}\theta_{V,k}$ and $\varphi_{jk}^{-1}\theta_{V,k}$ respectively. They are equal because $\varphi_{ik}=\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}$. Scheme descent faithfulness gives equality on $V$, and the chart equivalence gives equality on $X_i\times_XX_j$. Thus $\alpha:KB\simeq1$ is an isomorphism of descent-data functors, not just of their component modules.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), step (7), overlap compatibility of the counit; the displayed computation uses the original triple cocycle.

proof.text: For $M\in\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ apply the construction to $K(M)$. On every scheme test $T\to X$, the canonical pullback comparisons identify $b_i^*t^*M$ with $L_i(T,K(M))$, compatibly with their transitions. Scheme descent full faithfulness supplies a unique $\beta_T:t^*M\simeq H_T(K(M))$ preserving these identifications. The uniqueness calculation of Step 4 makes these isomorphisms compatible with every scheme map and natural in $M$. On etale charts they assemble to $\beta:M\simeq BK(M)$. Moreover $\alpha_{K(M)}K(\beta_M)=1$: on the covers $B_j(V)$ of charts $V\to X_i$, the formulas for $\eta$, $\theta$ and $\beta_T$ cancel to the identity; scheme descent and chart faithfulness give the equality before those covers. Consequently for compatible maps $a:K(M)\to K(N)$ the map $\beta_N^{-1}B(a)\beta_M$ pulls back to $a$; any other such map agrees by naturality of $\beta$ and faithfulness of the chartwise scheme comparisons. This proves full faithfulness. The isomorphisms $\alpha$ give essential surjectivity, proving the assertion.

source.place: Tag 04W8 (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), step (7), inverse identity and uniqueness of descended maps, expanded by 023T full faithfulness.

proof.text: If $X=\varnothing$, every $X_i$ is empty, and its small etale module category has just the zero module and its unique morphism: the empty covering forces sections to be the zero module. Thus both the descent category and $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ are terminal, including when $I$ is empty. For nonempty $X$, the covering cannot have empty index set; empty members impose only zero-module data and the same construction applies. No step required quasi-compactness, separatedness, Noetherian hypotheses, or finite generation.
